summary: Paul Groner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD at Yale University, later serving as a professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1982–2026).

Paul Hacker was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his doctorate at Humboldt University of Berlin and his habilitation at the University of Bonn. He held chairs at Bonn (1955–1963) and the University of Münster (1963–1978).

Paul Harrison is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Auckland and earned his PhD at Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana, later holding posts at Auckland, Canterbury, and Stanford.

Paul J. Griffiths works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at Oxford and Wisconsin under Minoru Kiyota, he held professorships at Notre Dame, Chicago, the University of Illinois Chicago (2000–2007), and Duke University (2008–2017).
Paul K. Nietupski specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Columbia University and held a post at John Carroll University (attested 2008).
Paul Kingsbury specializes in linguistics and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under the supervision of George Cardona (attested 2002).
Paul Kiparsky is a linguist and Indologist who studied at MIT under Morris Halle (~1962–1965). He later took up a post at Stanford University around 1984.

Paul L. Swanson works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University and earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota, later serving as a professor at Nanzan University (attested 1991–2009).

Paul Mendes-Flohr was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Brooklyn College and Brandeis University. He served as a director at Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1999–2006) and professor at the University of Chicago (~1999–2016).

Paul Mus specialized in Buddhist studies and religious studies, studying at the EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris. He held positions at the EFEO, École Pratique des Hautes Études, Collège de France (1946–1969), and Yale University.
Paul Passy was a linguist who studied under Ferdinand de Saussure (~1881–1891). He held an academic post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from around 1894 to 1913.

Paul Pelliot was a Sinologist and Tibetologist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Édouard Chavannes in Paris. He held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient and served as a professor at the Collège de France from 1909 to 1945.

Paul R. Brass was an Indologist and political scientist who studied at Harvard College, Harvard University, and the University of Chicago. He was a professor at the University of Washington from around 1967 to 2008.
Paul Regnaud was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1876) and held a faculty post at the University of Lyon from around 1879 to 1908.

Paul Ricœur was a philosopher and scholar of religion who studied at the University of Rennes and University of Paris. He held professorships at Strasbourg, the Faculty of Arts of Paris, Paris Nanterre, Louvain, and the University of Chicago.
Paul Rouzer is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Harvard University and the University of Minnesota (both attested in 2007).
Paul Tedesco was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna. He held research and teaching positions at Princeton University (~1944–1952) and Yale University (1943, 1952–1966).

Paul Thieme was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate and habilitation at Göttingen. He held professorships at Halle-Wittenberg (1941–1953), Frankfurt (1953), Yale (1954–1960), and the University of Tübingen (1960–1973).

Paul Tillich was a philosopher and theologian who studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, and Breslau. He held professorships at Marburg, Dresden, Leipzig, Frankfurt, Union Theological Seminary (1933–1955), Harvard (1955–1962), and Chicago (1962–1965).

Paul W. Kroll is a Sinologist who completed his studies at the University of Michigan (~1968–1976). Around 1979, he served as associate professor and department chair at the University of Colorado Boulder.
